generated.caption:
Imagine your business data suddenly locked, demanding a ransom. 🚨 China-linked hackers (Storm-1175) are deploying a *new* ransomware, StormEncryptor. This financially motivated group previously used Medusa ransomware and likely exploits vulnerabilities, such as the N-central flaw, to encrypt victim files.

generated.script: Heads up! China-linked hackers just dropped a dangerous new ransomware. The group, known as Storm-1175, is financially motivated and linked to China. They've unveiled StormEncryptor, a brand-new, previously undocumented ransomware strain. This isn't their old Medusa ransomware; StormEncryptor is written in C++ and tacks '.encrypted' onto your files. This shift means new defenses are needed, and reports suggest it's likely deploying via an N-central flaw. Protect yourself. Update your systems and enhance your security protocols immediately.

slides.body: Microsoft has disclosed that Storm-1175, a financially motivated threat actor linked to China, has deployed a previously undocumented ransomware strain called StormEncryptor. This new ransomware marks a shift from the adversary's previous use of Medusa ransomware. StormEncryptor is written in C++ and appends the file name extension .encrypted to compromised files. Organizations should be aware of this evolving threat from the China-linked group.
